quests.hint: Stress 'GRAND-fa-ther' on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: Long compound nouns like 'grandfather' usually keep strongest stress on the first part.
quests.textToSpeak: My grandfather tells the best stories at dinner.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'PLAN-ning' and keep 'a family' light and connected.
quests.explanation: The main verb carries stress while the following noun phrase flows quickly and lightly.
quests.textToSpeak: We are planning a family trip next month.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'JUST' to emphasize how recent the news is.
quests.explanation: Words like 'just' that add emphasis to timing often receive extra stress.
quests.textToSpeak: My cousin just got a new job in Boston.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'have been' to 'hav-bin' in fast speech.
quests.explanation: The present perfect auxiliary 'have been' often reduces in casual, connected speech.
quests.textToSpeak: I have been feeling much better this week.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'trying to' so it blends smoothly together.
quests.explanation: Verb plus 'to' combinations, like 'trying to,' often link closely in natural speech.
quests.textToSpeak: She is trying to eat more vegetables.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'DOC-tor' on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: Most two-syllable professional titles in English, like 'doctor,' stress the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: He needs to see a doctor about his cough.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Notice 'going to' may sound like 'gonna' in casual speech.
quests.explanation: As covered earlier, 'going to' often reduces to 'gonna' in relaxed conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: We are going to watch a new series tonight.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'pre-FERS' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The verb 'prefer' is stressed on the second syllable, unlike many other two-syllable verbs.
quests.textToSpeak: She prefers reading books to watching television.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'per-FORM-ing' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: Words built from 'perform' keep the stress on the second syllable across different forms.
quests.textToSpeak: The band is performing at the festival this weekend.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Keep 'are coming to' light and connected, leading into the stressed word 'visit.'
quests.explanation: Auxiliary verbs and 'to' stay light, letting the main action verb stand out.
quests.textToSpeak: My parents are coming to visit us this weekend.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'usually' to three quick beats, as practiced before.
quests.explanation: This is a good chance to reinforce the earlier pattern: 'usually' often shrinks to three syllables.
quests.textToSpeak: We usually have breakfast together on Sundays.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Link 'looking forward to' as one smooth phrase.
quests.explanation: Common expressions like 'looking forward to' are often said as a single connected unit.
quests.textToSpeak: I am looking forward to the holidays.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'ap-PLY-ing' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The verb 'apply' and its forms keep stress on the second syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: She is applying for a new position at work.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'dis-CUSS' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: Many two-syllable verbs of Latin origin, like 'discuss,' stress the second syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: We will discuss the budget at tomorrow's meeting.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'TRAIN-ing' on the first syllable, since 'train' is the root word.
quests.explanation: Gerunds keep the stress pattern of their base verb, just as 'training' follows 'train.'
quests.textToSpeak: He is training a new employee this week.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Notice the phrasal verb stress: SET-ting UP.
quests.explanation: In phrasal verbs, both the verb and the particle, like 'set up,' often carry stress.
quests.textToSpeak: I am setting up my new computer tonight.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'BACK-ing UP,' the phrasal verb pair.
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs like 'back up' typically stress both parts more evenly than single verbs.
quests.textToSpeak: She is backing up her files just in case.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'for the' quickly between the stressed words.
quests.explanation: Small grammatical words cluster together quickly between the more important content words.
quests.textToSpeak: We are waiting for the software update to finish.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Link 'getting used to' smoothly as one phrase.
quests.explanation: Common expressions like 'used to' are often pronounced as a single, fast unit in speech.
quests.textToSpeak: He is getting used to his new medication.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'STAR-ted' and 'GYM,' the key content words.
quests.explanation: In sentences describing a new habit, the verb of change and the activity usually carry stress.
quests.textToSpeak: She has started going to the gym regularly.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'MORE' to highlight the comparison.
quests.explanation: Comparative words like 'more' often get extra stress to highlight the contrast being made.
quests.textToSpeak: I am drinking more water than before.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 're-HEARS-ing' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The verb 'rehearse' and its forms are stressed on the second syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: They are rehearsing for the school play next week.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'STREAM-ing' on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: Single-syllable root verbs with -ing, like 'streaming,' keep the stress on that first part.
quests.textToSpeak: We are streaming a documentary about space tonight.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'to' quickly between 'learning' and 'play.'
quests.explanation: As practiced before, 'to' reduces to a light sound between two verbs.
quests.textToSpeak: She is learning to play the guitar this year.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'REN-o-vat-ing' on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: Many -ate verbs, like 'renovate,' keep primary stress on the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: We are renovating our kitchen this summer.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'a-BROAD' on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The word 'abroad' is stressed on the second syllable, unlike many similar adjectives.
quests.textToSpeak: My brother is studying abroad this semester.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'SAV-ing' and 'CAR,' the key content words.
quests.explanation: The action of saving and the goal of the action usually both receive stress.
quests.textToSpeak: I am saving money for a new car.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'BAL-anc-ing' on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: This wraps up the Easy level: -ing forms typically follow the stress of their base verb.
quests.textToSpeak: She is balancing work and family this year.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Reduce 'have been' quickly before the stressed word 'planning.'
quests.explanation: Present perfect continuous forms often reduce the auxiliary while stressing the main verb.
quests.textToSpeak: We have been planning this trip for months.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.

quests.hint: Stress 'PROUD' and 'FAR' to show genuine feeling.
quests.explanation: Emotional words like 'proud' benefit from clear stress and a warmer tone to convey sincerity.
quests.textToSpeak: I am proud of how far we have come.
quests.instruction: Listen and repeat the sentence exactly as you hear it.
